data: Principles of Programming Languages is a deep dive into analytical foundations of programming languages, their design, and implementation. These foundations have proved to be of enduring importance, and hold the key to understanding future developments in programming languages. These foundations are centered around the semantics of program elements, which reflect how program elements are interpreted as a program is executed. This course will use interpretation of programs as the approach to learn these principles - a “mental model” - of programming languages. It will draw on the PLAI (“Programming Languages: Application and Interpretation”) body of  material and will be  taught using Racket, a dialect of Scheme. In this course, “language” does not refer to “surface structure”, also known as “syntax”, but will focus on the “semantics” or meaning of programs
